The first player writes a list of positive integers not greater than \( 25 \), not necessarily different, such that their sum is at least \( 200 \). The second player wins if he can select some of these numbers so that their sum \( S \) satisfies the condition \( 200-N \leq S \leq 200+N \). What is the smallest value of \( N \) for which the second player has a winning strategy?", "assumptions": [], "domain": "baltic_mo", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "target": {"node_id": "n11", "version": 1}, "target_node": {"text": "#### Case 1: Total Sum $ S \leq 210 $

If the total sum of the list is **less than or equal to 210**, then Player 2 can simply choose the **entire list**, and the sum will be in the range $[200, 210]$, which is within $[200 - 10, 200 + 10]$.   $$
  200 - N \leq S \leq 200 + N
  $$
- The goal is to find the **smallest** such $ N $ for which **Player 2 always has a winning strategy**, regardless of how Player 1 chooses the list.", "scope": [], "depends_on": []}, {"node_id": "n10", "version": 1, "claim": "The text announces the intended universal upper-bound argument for N equal to 10.", "text": "---
